items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Roger Sequel told me, I said I'm going to take up Sillinger. He said, man, you don't need it.

ctx.x: Roger Sequel told me, I said I'm going to take up Sillinger. He said, man, you don't need it. You are writing all this music and you need some Sillinger. I said well, everybody else is taking and he said, they have no imagination. You see, one thing I did while I was in the theatre, like that, I would never listen to anybody else's arrangements, scared I'd put something in. Hear something about theirs. I'd sit up all night and write a number. I remember we had a show at the Lafayette Theatre and Carey was the…
So I said, go ahead, it's your show and I tore up all the music. Then I had to go back and write it.. That's why I'm blind today.
